world: Old rural Norway on an autumn evening. A narrow dirt road winds between hazel bushes and birches, past stubble fields and grey stone walls. The boy cracks hazelnuts as he walks; the worm-eaten nut is an ordinary brown hazelnut with one tiny round wormhole, which he plugs with a little whittled wooden peg. By the road stands the smithy: a low log building with a turf roof and a stone chimney, a wide open door, a glowing forge with leather bellows, a big black anvil on a tree stump, and a rack of hammers from tiny to huge, the biggest a great sledgehammer as long as a man's leg.
palette: Late October at dusk: bare birches holding their last rust-brown leaves, hazel bushes gone yellow, a cold violet-and-rose sky with the first star, frost starting in the ruts of the road and long blue shadows. Inside the smithy: the orange glow of the forge, sparks and swirling dust against sooty dark walls.

cast.look: A scruffy, cheeky boy of about fourteen, small and wiry, with a round, sun-browned face, a turned-up nose, bright black eyes, a wide, mischievous grin and straight dark-brown hair cut in a thick, blunt fringe down to his eyebrows. He wears an open, much-mended red waistcoat over a baggy, untucked homespun smock, short brown trousers frayed at the hems and scuffed ankle boots, and every pocket bulges with hazelnuts.
cast.portrait: Background: the dirt road between yellow hazel bushes at dusk.

simplified.name: Gutten
simplified.description: En kvikk og nysgjerrig gutt som bruker et enkelt triks for å fange fanden i en nøtt.

english.name: The Boy
english.description: A quick-witted traveler who cracks nuts on the road and confidently tricks the Devil into a trap.

cast.look: A small, skinny devil about half the height of a man, with dusty, matte brick-red skin, a narrow, pointed face with a sharp, beardless chin, narrow, sly green eyes under thin arched eyebrows, a wide, smug grin, big pointed ears and two tiny stubby horns like thorns. He has thin arms, knobbly knees, long bare feet with curling toes and a long thin tail ending in a black tuft like a paintbrush, and wears only short, ragged brown breeches held up by a string.
cast.portrait: Background: a hazel bush by the road in the violet dusk.

simplified.name: Fanden
simplified.description: Stolt og selvsikker, men lar seg lure når han vil bevise at han kan gjøre seg bitteliten.

english.name: The Devil
english.description: A boastful, supernatural being who says he can make himself small enough to squeeze through a pinhole, and falls for the boy’s challenge.

cast.look: A stocky old blacksmith of about sixty-five, short and broad, with huge, sooty forearms, a wide, soot-smudged face, crinkly brown eyes under thick grey eyebrows and a long, bushy charcoal-grey beard singed at the tips. He has a fuzz of short grey hair, and small round wire spectacles sit pushed up on his forehead. He wears a heavy, scorched leather apron over a faded red homespun shirt with rolled-up sleeves, sooty black trousers and big wooden clogs.
cast.portrait: Background: the glowing forge inside the smithy.

simplified.name: Smeden
simplified.description: En sterk håndverker som blir irritert når nøtta nekter å sprekke og ender med å bruke slegga.

english.name: The Blacksmith
english.description: A practical craftsman whose growing frustration leads him to use a massive sledge, unleashing the Devil’s explosive escape.

cover.prompt: On a narrow dirt road between yellow hazel bushes at dusk, the Boy stands cracking hazelnuts, holding up one nut with a tiny wormhole between finger and thumb and grinning. Beside him, the Devil has just stepped out from behind a hazel bush, puffing out his chest with a sly, boastful grin, his tufted tail curling up behind him. Far along the road, the low log smithy glows orange, with smoke rising from its chimney.

simplified.caption: Gutten knakk nøtter, og akkurat da møtte han Fanden.
simplified.alt: Gutten står på veien mellom hasselbuskene og holder opp ei nøtt. Ved siden av ham har Fanden kommet fram bak en busk med et lurt glis. Langt borte lyser smia.

english.caption: The boy was cracking nuts, and at that very moment he met the Devil.
english.alt: The boy stands on the road between the hazel bushes, holding up a nut. Beside him, the Devil has stepped out from behind a bush with a sly grin. Far away, the smithy glows.

illustrations.prompt: A close, low view on the road between the hazel bushes at sunset: the Boy crouches and holds up a hazelnut between finger and thumb, with a little whittled wooden peg ready in his other hand and a sly grin. The Devil has shrunk to the size of a beetle and is wriggling head first into the tiny wormhole in the shell, so that only his thin legs and tufted tail still stick out. Low amber light slants through the leaves.

simplified.caption: Han ble mindre og mindre og krøp inn gjennom markhullet.
simplified.alt: Gutten sitter på huk og holder opp ei nøtt, med en liten pinne klar i den andre hånda. Fanden er blitt bitteliten og kryper inn gjennom markhullet, så bare beina og halen stikker ut.

english.caption: He made himself smaller and smaller and wriggled in through the wormhole.
english.alt: The boy crouches, holding up a nut with a little peg ready in his other hand. The Devil has shrunk tiny and is wriggling in through the wormhole, so only his legs and tail stick out.

illustrations.prompt: Inside the smithy just after the bang: half the turf roof has flown off, and through the gaping hole the violet evening sky shows, with dust and clods of turf still raining down and a thin streak of sooty smoke curling away into the sky. The Smith stands frozen by the anvil with the great sledgehammer in his hands, staring at the shattered nutshell. The Boy stands calmly beside him with his hands on his hips. The forge glows orange.

simplified.anchor: Smeden ble stående og glo på ambolten.
simplified.caption: Smeden ble stående og glo på ambolten.
simplified.alt: Halve taket på smia har fløyet av, og støv drysser ned. Smeden står med storslegga og glor på ambolten, og gutten står rolig ved siden av med hendene i siden.

english.anchor: The blacksmith stood staring at the wreckage on the anvil.
english.caption: The blacksmith stood staring at the wreckage on the anvil.
english.alt: Half the roof of the smithy has flown off, and dust is raining down. The blacksmith stands with the great sledgehammer, staring at the anvil, while the boy stands calmly beside him.
